title: Crematorium proposed at Victoria Street funeral home
subtitle: Short meeting with one public hearing; site-specific zoning, 80-metre buffer from homes, and provincial notice requirements.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held a short meeting with a single public hearing item. It considered a zoning change for 1014 Victoria Street North, a former home hardware store that is being converted into a funeral home.

The committee recommended approving the amendment, which would add a crematorium as a permitted use alongside the funeral home {{vote:m1}}. The commercial zoning stays in place, with a site-specific rule that the crematorium must be at least 80 metres from residential lands. The recommendation also asks Council to give approval under the Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, and directs staff to notify the provincial registrar and the owner and to publish notice in The Record.

For residents, the item matters because it sets where a crematorium may operate and builds in a separation from nearby homes. Because this is a committee, the recommendation goes to Council, which was to consider it later the same day. Residents who did not speak or write before Council decides may lose the right to appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

decisions.item: Zoning change for 1014 Victoria Street North
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving a zoning by-law amendment that adds a crematorium use to the funeral home site, with a minimum 80-metre setback from residential lands.
The committee recommended that Council give approval under Section 83(3) of the Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act to establish the crematorium.
The committee recommended directing staff to send the Council decision to the provincial registrar and the owner, and to publish notice in The Record.

debate: Staff said the proposal is consistent with provincial, regional and city planning policies, and that the 80-metre setback provides an appropriate buffer to residential lands.
Staff noted the funeral home is already permitted under current zoning and site plan approval has been issued, so the amendment only adds the crematorium use.
The applicant's planning consultant supported the staff recommendation and said there were no concerns with the report or the draft by-law.
One councillor, who moved the item, said it was good work by staff and appropriate development that would be good for the local economy. No questions were raised and no residents spoke.
